C-KERNEL-PERSISTENCE-RECOVERY-MODEL-2026.Title: Persistence and Recovery Model v1: Crash-Safe State, Transactional Outbox, Durable Journal, Blob Storage and Persistent Scheduler Primitives

Constraints.Constraint: Production persistence remains behind generic kernel storage contracts; database-specific handles and product-domain types do not cross the plugin boundary.
Event transport, audit storage, and derived indexes remain separate from authoritative application state; event sourcing is opt-in per bounded domain.
Storage-open and durability failures are explicit and never silently fall back to in-memory storage.
Existing M0.1-M0.4 contracts and repository-owned Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, and ProvingSlice suite names remain stable.
In-memory implementations remain available for deterministic unit and contract tests; production proving evidence uses the selected production backend.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh local evidence covers production persistence, process-kill recovery, S1 continuity and authority discontinuity; hosted CI remains unverified until a named run exists.

Preconditions.Precondition: M0.4 — Capability RPC and Event Transport — Done.
Repository-owned CI baseline exists and future persistence acceptance tests must be reachable through the existing stable CI suites.

RoadmapAlignment.Postcondition: После успешного завершения active implementation milestone становится M0.6 — Stable IPC and WASM Component Boundary.

ArchitecturalInvariants.Invariant: EVERY PERSISTED DOMAIN HAS EXACTLY ONE AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE OF TRUTH.
EVENT JOURNAL IS NOT APPLICATION STATE.
AUDIT LOG IS NOT APPLICATION STATE.
DERIVED INDEX IS NEVER AUTHORITATIVE STATE.
A COMMITTED STATE MUTATION MUST SURVIVE PROCESS CRASH.
AN UNCOMMITTED STATE MUTATION MUST NOT APPEAR AFTER RECOVERY.
CAS SEMANTICS MUST SURVIVE PROCESS RESTART.
STATE AND REQUIRED NOTIFICATION INTENT MUST COMMIT ATOMICALLY WHEN THE DOMAIN REQUIRES BOTH TO SURVIVE.
OUTBOX DELIVERY MAY BE AT-LEAST-ONCE; EXACTLY-ONCE EXTERNAL EFFECTS ARE NOT CLAIMED.
OUTBOX REDELIVERY REUSES THE SAME LOGICAL EVENT IDENTITY.
PROCESS CRASH MUST NEVER TURN AN UNKNOWN EXTERNAL SIDE EFFECT INTO A CLAIMED SUCCESS.
LARGE OR SECRET PAYLOADS DO NOT ENTER AUDIT LOG BY DEFAULT.
PRODUCTION STORAGE IMPLEMENTATION IS REPLACEABLE; STORAGE SEMANTICS ARE NOT.
STORAGE FAILURE MUST BE EXPLICIT. SILENT FALLBACK TO IN-MEMORY STORAGE IS FORBIDDEN.
BACKUP IS NOT VALID UNTIL RESTORE HAS BEEN PROVEN.

Goals.Goal: Выбрать и документировать production persistence boundary.
Реализовать production StateBackend с crash-safe atomic transactions и optimistic CAS.
Реализовать transactional outbox для согласованной state mutation + notification intent.
Реализовать production EventJournal для M0.4 Durable delivery contract.
Реализовать content-addressed blob store для immutable large payloads.
Добавить deterministic recovery failpoints и real child-process kill tests.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Telemetry backend implementation beyond required contracts.
Automatic event sourcing for all state.
Automatic retry of arbitrary external actions.
Automatic blob garbage collection across unknown domains.

RequiredADR.Requirement: ADR MUST explicitly explain why event sourcing is or is not selected for each persisted domain introduced by this change.
Event sourcing MUST NOT be selected merely because an event transport already exists.

Domain.name: NotificationIntent
Domain.Mutation: Atomic with owning state transaction where required

Domain.name: DurableEventTransport
Domain.Note: Source of truth only for transport acceptance/replay semantics, not for application state.

Domain.name: DerivedIndex
Domain.Rule: Index must always be rebuildable from authoritative domain state.

ProductionBackendSelection.Rule: Change MUST land at least one real production storage implementation.
ProductionBackendSelection.Candidate: Content-addressed blobs may use filesystem-backed storage independent from the transactional metadata database.
ProductionBackendSelection.Rule: If SQLite is rejected, ADR must provide measured or architectural evidence and the selected alternative must satisfy the same acceptance criteria.
Database-specific types MUST NOT leak through kernel/plugin contracts.
worldline-kernel MUST NOT expose SQLite connection handles to plugins.
ProductionBackendSelection.PreferredDependencyDirection:
host/storage implementation -> kernel storage contracts
kernel !-> product persistence domain

StateBackendV1.Rule: State values remain opaque bytes to the storage backend.
State backend must not infer domain semantics from state keys.
Ordinary transaction may not mutate schema metadata.
Stale pre-crash transaction identity cannot be resurrected after restart.

DurabilityContract.Requirement: A successful commit acknowledgement means the implementation has crossed its documented crash-durability boundary.
Process termination after successful commit must not lose committed state under supported filesystem/storage assumptions.

Crash before commit acknowledgement may result only in: - previous committed state; - or new fully committed state if commit actually crossed durability boundary before termination.
Torn logical transaction is forbidden.
If SQLite is selected, durability-related PRAGMA/configuration is explicit and covered by ADR rather than relying on library defaults.

PersistentFormat.Requirement: Storage layout/database schema has explicit format version.
Unsupported newer format fails closed with explicit error.

TransactionalOutbox.Purpose: Prevent committed domain mutation from losing a required notification because the process crashed between state commit and event publication.
TransactionalOutbox.Invariant: State mutation and corresponding Pending outbox record are committed in one atomic storage transaction.
Plugin payload cannot forge trusted producer/correlation/authority metadata.
Outbox admission authority is established at original operation admission.
TransactionalOutbox.Rule: Restart delivery is completion of previously admitted durable intent; it is not interpreted as a new arbitrary plugin publication.
Subscription authority is still evaluated according to event delivery semantics.
Crash after publish but before marking Delivered may cause redelivery.
Redelivery MUST reuse the original EventId.
Exactly-once subscriber side effects are NOT guaranteed.
Outbox delivery state itself is persisted.

EventJournalV1.Purpose: Replace M0.4 test-only in-memory durable journal with a production crash-safe implementation.
EventJournalV1.Invariant: Event journal is NOT automatically read to rebuild installation state.
Event journal does not become a universal domain database.
EventJournalV1.Rule: M0.5 does not promise global ordering across producers.

AuditStore.Purpose: Persist selected security/lifecycle/control-plane facts that require durable audit without storing arbitrary RPC/event payloads.
AuditStore.Rule: Audit failure policy is explicit per record class.
Audit log does not determine current authoritative runtime/state.

BlobStore.Purpose: Store immutable large payloads outside transactional metadata rows.
BlobStore.BlobId: Versioned digest identity chosen by ADR.

Requirements.Requirement: Partial write never becomes visible as complete blob.
Crash may leave removable temporary files only.

BlobStore.Rule: BlobId is content identity, not authority.
Knowledge of BlobId does not automatically grant plugin read access.
Cross-domain garbage collection is deferred until ownership/reference policy exists.

SchedulerPrimitives.Purpose: Provide persistent generic work-state semantics without implementing product background tasks or a distributed scheduler.
SchedulerPrimitives.Invariant: Running job found after host restart is not silently assumed Completed.
Running job found after host restart is not blindly re-executed unless its recovery policy allows it.
SchedulerPrimitives.Rule: Unknown external effect outcome becomes Interrupted/explicitly incomplete, never synthetic success.
Scheduler state is authoritative in JobStore, not inferred from events.
M0.5 scheduler does not own browser/agent/workspace task semantics.

BackupRestore.Requirement: Production persistence implementation exposes a consistent backup/snapshot operation or documents the supported external mechanism.
Backup created while database is active must be transactionally consistent.
Restore is tested into a fresh storage location.
Restored store validates format/schema before boot.

RetentionRedactionDeletion.Requirement: Every store class documents its default retention policy.
Audit/event/blob stores do not inherit retention policy from each other.
State deletion and audit retention are separate concepts.
Sensitive fields are excluded at write time where possible rather than relying on future redaction.
Automatic compaction must preserve authoritative semantics.
RetentionRedactionDeletion.Rule: M0.5 may use conservative no-auto-delete defaults where product ownership rules do not yet exist.

RecoveryTesting.Purpose: Prove persistence against actual process termination rather than only returning injected errors in the same process.
RecoveryTesting.Requirement: Add a child-process recovery harness or equivalent executable acceptance fixture.
Parent process can force termination at named deterministic persistence failpoints.
Failpoint mechanism is test-only and cannot be enabled accidentally in production build.

RequiredCrashPoints.CrashPoint: after state + outbox commit before publish
after event publish before outbox Delivered mark
after job marked Running before completion

RecoveryTesting.Rule: Recovery assertion runs in a new process/host instance.
Tests must not rely solely on graceful Drop/destructor execution.

RecoveryOutcomes.Outcome: Operation is durably present and internally consistent.
State is committed and durable outbox proves notification still requires delivery.
Durable scheduler/control-plane metadata proves operation started but no final outcome can be established.
RecoveryOutcomes.Invariant: Recovery must never invent a fifth ambiguous success state.

S1PersistenceProvingSlice.Purpose: Upgrade existing S1 from restart evidence to production persistence/recovery evidence.
S1PersistenceProvingSlice.RequiredPath: fresh persistent host profile -> installation creation -> runtime activation -> explicit authority -> capability RPC -> authoritative state mutation -> transactionally enqueue observation intent -> commit -> crash before outbox delivery -> new host process -> recover committed state -> fresh RuntimeId -> no inherited runtime authority -> recover Pending outbox record -> publish same EventId -> observer receives event -> mark outbox delivered -> second restart -> no lost committed state -> no accidental duplicate pending intent
S1PersistenceProvingSlice.Requirement: S1 production path uses selected production StateBackend.
InMemoryStateBackend remains available for unit tests but cannot satisfy M0.5 exit criterion.

RequiredTests.Test: Production backend survives clean host restart.
Successful committed state survives process kill.
Kill before commit exposes only previous committed state.
Transaction never recovers partially written key set.
StateRevision remains monotonic after restart.
CAS conflict is detected after independent process reopen.
Stale transaction cannot commit after restart.
Migration success survives process kill after commit.
Interrupted migration recovers to explicit retryable state.
Interrupted uninstall remains explicitly recoverable.
State mutation + outbox record commit atomically.
Crash after state/outbox commit before publication loses neither.
Restart dispatcher delivers pending outbox record.
Outbox redelivery preserves EventId.
Crash after publish before Delivered mark may redeliver but does not create a new logical event identity.
Outbox implementation does not claim exactly-once subscriber effect.
Production EventJournal survives restart.
EventJournal replay cursor survives restart.
Event journal corruption is explicit failure.
Event journal is not consulted to reconstruct installation state.
Audit store persists selected metadata facts.
Audit records contain no raw state/RPC/event payload in protected cases.
Blob put is idempotent by content.
Partial blob write is never visible as valid blob.
Blob corruption is detected on verification/read.
Possession of BlobId does not bypass authority layer.
Pending/Waiting scheduler jobs survive restart.
Running job at crash recovers as Interrupted or according to explicit safe recovery policy.
Manual recovery policy never automatically re-executes crashed job.
Cancelled job remains cancelled after restart.
Deadline/wakeup metadata survives restart.
Consistent backup can be restored into fresh profile.
Restored store rejects unsupported newer format.
S1 production persistence proving slice passes.
Existing S0 and M0.1-M0.4 acceptance suites remain green.

StaticArchitectureChecks.Requirement: worldline-kernel does not expose database-specific handles or types.
Product domain types do not enter generic persistence contracts.
Event transport is not used as StateBackend implementation.
Audit store is not used as StateBackend implementation.
No production persistence path silently instantiates InMemoryStateBackend after open/configuration failure.
Blob storage path is bounded to configured profile/storage root.
Recovery test failpoints cannot be enabled in normal production feature set.

SecurityRequirements.Requirement: Storage path/profile root is host configuration, not arbitrary plugin input.
Plugins do not receive raw database/file handles.
Installation state remains installation-bound after persistence.
Runtime state lease semantics remain unchanged.
Host restart does not restore runtime grants.
Outbox persistence does not become authority persistence.
Durable event producer identity is immutable once admitted.
Blob hash/path traversal cannot escape configured blob root.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: ADR-PERSISTENCE-RECOVERY-V1 exists and assigns one source of truth to each introduced persistence domain.
A production StateBackend exists.
Production state transactions are crash-atomic.
CAS/revision semantics survive process restart.
Production backend never silently degrades to in-memory state.
State + required notification intent can commit atomically.
Outbox pending records survive crash.
Redelivery preserves logical EventId.
Exactly-once external delivery is not claimed.
Production EventJournal survives restart and supports replay cursor.
Event journal remains separate from authoritative application state.
Selective audit persistence exists without raw payload logging by default.
Content-addressed blob store performs atomic publication and corruption detection.
Blob identity creates no authority.
Persistent job state survives restart.
Crash while Running never becomes synthetic Completed.
Unsafe job replay requires explicit recovery policy.
Backup is accepted only after successful restore validation.
Process-kill tests cover all required critical persistence points.
S1 uses production persistence in at least one required end-to-end path.
S1 proves state continuity and runtime authority discontinuity across crash.
Existing M0.1-M0.4 semantics remain green.
Existing repository-owned CI suite names remain stable.
Persistence/recovery acceptance is reachable through repository-owned CI.
ROADMAP marks M0.5 Done and M0.6 Next only after process-kill recovery evidence exists.

ImplementationGuidance.Guidance: DO NOT start by replacing every in-memory store at once.
First freeze persistence semantics and source-of-truth decisions in ADR.
Implement production StateBackend before scheduler/blob expansion.
Keep InMemory implementations for fast deterministic unit tests.
Production and in-memory implementations MUST pass the same semantic contract suite where applicable.
Prefer separate storage implementation crate over importing database code throughout kernel modules.
Do not put opaque large blobs directly into audit rows merely because the database can store BLOB columns.
Do not build a generic event-sourcing framework in this change.
Do not create a second event bus for outbox dispatch.
Outbox dispatcher feeds the existing M0.4 event transport.
Do not implement unsafe automatic retry for an Interrupted scheduler job.
Prefer deterministic child-process failpoints over timing-based "kill after sleep" recovery tests.
CI workflow YAML remains orchestration only. New recovery logic belongs in repository-owned tests/tools.

SuggestedExecutionOrder.Step: Write ADR-PERSISTENCE-RECOVERY-V1 and select production backend.
Run existing StateBackend contract suite against both in-memory and production backends.
Add child-process crash harness and state commit failpoints.
Implement transactional outbox integrated with state transaction boundary.
Implement production EventJournal behind existing M0.4 contract.
Implement persistent JobStore and minimal scheduler recovery semantics.
Upgrade S1 to production persistence/crash path.
Route recovery tests through existing repository-owned CI suites without renaming the stable leaf suites.
Update GRACE durable projection and ROADMAP only after evidence exists.

ReviewQuestions.Question: Для каждого persisted table/file можно ли назвать ровно один bounded domain и source of truth?
Используется ли где-либо event log для восстановления mutable state без явного event-sourcing ADR?
Может ли successful commit потеряться после process kill?
Может ли torn transaction стать видимой?
Может ли crash между state commit и notification потерять notification?
Может ли outbox retry создать новый EventId?
Есть ли где-нибудь ложное exactly-once обещание?
Может ли plugin получить raw database connection или filesystem storage root?
Может ли storage open failure незаметно перейти на in-memory backend?
Содержит ли audit store raw sensitive payloads?
Может ли Running job после crash автоматически стать Completed?
Может ли unsafe external action быть автоматически повторено?
Проверяли ли backup настоящим restore?
Process-kill tests действительно убивают process, или всего лишь возвращают injected Result::Err?
Не внедряем ли мы преждевременно browser/workspace persistence в kernel?

FailureConditions.Failure: Production state backend теряет acknowledged commit после supported crash.
Production failure silently falls back to memory.
Event bus становится authoritative state database.
Audit log становится authoritative state database.
State commit и required notification могут рассинхронизироваться без explicit recoverable record.
Crash-running job silently retries unsafe work.
Raw database/storage handle пересекает plugin boundary.
Process recovery is tested only through graceful shutdown.
Product-domain persistence types leak into worldline-kernel.

CIIntegration.Invariant: Stable repository-owned leaf suite names remain: Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, ProvingSlice.
CIIntegration.Requirement: Persistence unit/contract/recovery tests are integrated under existing suites rather than creating ad-hoc GitHub-only commands.
Production S1 crash path belongs to ProvingSlice.
Architecture/storage boundary guards belong to ArchitectureSecurity.
Backend contract tests belong to Correctness.

VerificationExpectations.Expectation: Repository-owned CI remains canonical verification entrypoint.
Production storage backend is exercised by process restart/kill tests.
In-memory and production backend implementations satisfy shared semantic contract tests.
S1 passes production persistence recovery path.
No browser, agent, UI or model persistence types enter kernel.

ExitCriteria.Criterion: Worldline has one production crash-safe persistence implementation.
Authoritative installation state survives process crash with atomic CAS semantics.
Committed state and required notification intent cannot be lost between each other.
Pending notification survives restart and preserves EventId on redelivery.
Durable event journal has real crash persistence without becoming domain state.
Audit storage remains selective and metadata-oriented.
Blob store provides atomic content-addressed immutable storage.
Persistent job state distinguishes Completed from Interrupted after crash.
Recovery behavior is proven using real process termination.
Every persisted domain explicitly names its source of truth.
S1 demonstrates production boot -> mutation -> crash -> recovery -> observation -> restart.
Kernel is ready for M0.6 native-process/WASM boundaries without another persistence semantics redesign.

Assumptions.Assumption: Single-host local persistence is sufficient for M0.
One Worldline profile owns its configured storage root.
Persistent storage is local by default.
Cloud sync, if ever added, will be a separate capability/domain.
SQLite is the initial production candidate, not a public ABI.
In-memory storage remains useful for tests.
